intended_answer: The coherent signal bearer is defined exactly as the one participant whose six evidence statuses—relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol—produce the incident’s accepted iterated modular checksum under the local rules. No participant is selected or implied here; the formalizer and deterministic code must compute the answer.
premise: After a sandstorm strands a five-person desert expedition among buried relay pylons, the team discovers that a chain of emergency beacons has been transmitting corrupted fragments of one distress call. Each fragment records clues about who contacted whom, when actions occurred, what caused each beacon’s failure, where equipment was moved, the order in which signals were relayed, and which transmission protocol was used. The expedition’s analysts must reconcile the field logs, beacon traces, map data, and recovery timeline into one accepted incident record. Under the expedition’s local rules, every participant receives six evidence statuses—relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol—and those statuses are fed into an iterated modular checksum. The locally defined concept “coherent signal bearer” is the one participant whose six evidence statuses produce the incident’s accepted iterated modular checksum. The team’s task is to determine that participant without relying on names, job titles, or narrative prominence.
setting_summary: A desert expedition decodes a chain of emergency beacons after a sandstorm disrupts its route. Five participants are evaluated against cross-checked relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol evidence from the beacon chain and field records.
target_question: Which participant is the coherent signal bearer?
